data.name: Aufa
data.gender_notes: Aufa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'aufa', meaning 'worshipper' or 'one who performs prayers'. A fitting name for a girl who is deeply devoted to her faith. The name Aufa carries the meaning “Worshipper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aufa usually hope their child will grow to embody worshipper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name filled with devotion and piety.
data.etymology: Aufa belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Worshipper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aufa total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: عوفا
in_arabic.meaning: اسم عربي يرمز للعفة والإنضباط والصبر
in_arabic.long_meaning: يعود اسم عوفا إلى أصل عربي يرمز للأنضباط والصبر والصالحية، وقد تم اختياره من قبل العديد من المسلمين لتمثيل قيمهم الدينية، ويتميز اسم عوفا بالعفة والانتماء للدين، ويعد من أسماء الرجال في الإسلام التي تميزها الصبر والانضباط.

In modern times, the name Aufa is used in many Muslim cultures, and it is seen as a symbol of self-control and discipline.

Aufa is mentioned in several Hadiths, including one where she interceded on behalf of the Muslims to the Prophet, asking him to pray for forgiveness for them. Another Hadith relates that when the Prophet was on his deathbed, he requested that Aufa be present to comfort him and recite the Quran to him.

historical_references.reference: Aufa bint Umar was a prominent female companion of the Prophet Muhammad. She was a sister of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, the second caliph of Islam. Aufa is known for her piety and her generosity towards the poor. She was one of the first women to accept Islam and was a close friend of Aisha bint Abu Bakr, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad. Aufa is mentioned in various Hadiths, including one where she gave her ring to the Prophet as a gift and he returned it to her, saying that it would bring her blessings.
historical_references.time_period: 622-632 CE, during the early years of Islam in Medina.
historical_references.context: Acceptance of Islam and generosity towards the poor
